description: Sampler that records what is patched into it, cuts the recording into slices, and plays them back

params.text: Starts recording on the first press and stops on the second, keeping what was recorded
Sets where in the sample playback starts
Sets how much of the sample is played from that start point
Steps through the three ways a slice is read: forwards, backwards, and ping-pong
Sets how fast the sample is read, -4 to +4 times, so the lower half of its travel plays the sample backwards
Fades the ends of the loop in and out, up to half its length, which takes the click off a loop point
Switches what a recording does when it stops: replacing everything recorded before, or adding to the end of it as a new slice
Picks which slice is played, across however many slices the sample has been cut into
Clears the recording and every slice marker with it
Sets how loud a jump in level has to be to count as a transient when the sample is cut up automatically

inputs.text: A trigger here starts playing the slice from its start point, and while anything is patched here playing is trigger-driven
A gate here plays the slice for as long as it is held, and it is only used when nothing is patched to the trigger jack
Added to the start point, 10V being the whole sample
Added to the loop length, 10V being the whole sample
Steps the reading mode on, 0V to 10V across forwards, backwards and ping-pong
Added to the speed, a volt for each 1 of the ratio
A trigger here starts or stops recording
Added to the fade length, 10V being its whole range
Added to the slice number, 10V reaching the last slice
A trigger here clears the recording and every slice marker

outputs.text: The left channel being played back
The right channel being played back
A 10V pulse when the slice reaches its end

notes: the module comes up empty: record something into it with the REC button, or load a sample with Load sample from the right-click menu or by dropping a wav or aiff file onto the panel
the slice items in the menu work on the point last clicked in the waveform, so click the display to pick a point and then choose the item
drag up and down on the waveform to zoom and sideways to scroll, holding shift while dragging to zoom faster; shift and right-click on the waveform opens the module's own menu
shift-click the transient threshold trimpot to cut the sample at its transients, which is what the Detect transients menu item does
menu: Delete slice — takes the slice the waveform was last clicked in out of the sample, audio and all
Delete slice marker — removes the slice marker before the point the waveform was last clicked at
Add slice marker — puts a slice marker at the point the waveform was last clicked at
Detect transients — cuts the sample into slices at every jump in level above the transient threshold
Load sample — opens a wav or aiff file and loads it in place of the recording
Save sample — writes what has been recorded out as a wav file
